message.content:
**Uno – Basic Rules** | Item | Description | |------|-------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are earned by winning rounds and are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”), plus 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face down as the draw pile.
• Turn the top card of the draw pile face up to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two,” the first player draws two cards and loses their turn). | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a “Reverse” changes direction). On a turn, a player may play one card or draw from the draw pile. | | **Playing a Card** | A card can be played if:
• It matches the color of the top discard card.
• It matches the number/symbol of the top discard card.
• It is a Wild card (can be played on any card).
• It is a Wild Draw Four (can be played only if the player has no other playable card; otherwise, the next player may challenge). | | **Action Cards** | • **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Wild** – Player chooses the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Same as Wild, but next player draws four cards and skips their turn. | | **Drawing** | If a player cannot play a card, they must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card is playable, they may play it immediately; otherwise, the turn ends. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When a player has only one card left, they must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. Failure to do so results in a penalty: the player must draw two cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all of their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards remaining in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Draw Two, Skip, Reverse = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until a player reaches the target score (usually 500). | --- ### Variations & House Rules | Variation | What It Changes | |-----------|-----------------| | **Stacking** | Players may stack “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” cards on top of each other, forcing the next player to draw the cumulative total unless they can stack again. | | **No Challenge** | Some groups allow “Wild Draw Four” to be played at any time, eliminating the challenge rule. | | **Custom Decks** | Players can add extra cards or create themed decks. | | **Speed Uno** | A faster variant where players must play within a time limit. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep Track of Colors** – If you’re low on cards, try to keep a variety of colors to avoid being stuck with a single color you can’t play. 2. **Use Action Cards Strategically** – Save “Draw Two” or “Reverse” for when you’re about to win or to disrupt opponents. 3. **Watch Opponents’ Hands** – If you see someone playing a “Wild” or “Wild Draw Four,” they likely have no matching color. Enjoy your game!
